Telegram bot template: aiogram 3 + Django 5/ORM + Celery. Starter scaffold; functionality is intentionally minimal (`/start` and user tracking).

```sh
cp .env.example .env  # Then edit .env with your values
uv run python manage.py migrate
uv run python manage.py createsuperuser
uv run python manage.py runserver
uv run python main.py
uv run celery -A config worker --loglevel=info
uv run python manage.py makemigrations
uv run python manage.py test
uv run python manage.py createsuperuser
uv run python manage.py shell
```

`.env`: `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `DJANGO_SECRET_KEY` required; `CELERY_BROKER_URL` configures Redis; `START_COMMAND_MESSAGE` customizes `/start`.

`main.py` initializes Django ORM, configures aiogram Bot/Dispatcher, registers middleware/routes, and starts polling. `config/` provides Django settings, `dj-database-url` (SQLite default), Celery, and admin. `bot/` contains `models.py` (`TelegramUser`), `aiogram/handlers.py` (`/start`), `aiogram/middlewares.py` (`UserTrackingMiddleware`), and placeholder `tasks.py`.

Middleware automatically saves/updates users for every interaction. Bot DB operations use Django’s sync-to-async pattern. Add handlers in `bot/aiogram/handlers.py` or separate routers included in `main.py:42`; add models in `bot/models.py` and register in `bot/admin.py`; implement Celery tasks in `bot/tasks.py` using the `<REDACTED_USER>_task` decorator. Add environment variables to `.env.example`, access via `config/settings.py`.

Uses `uv` for dependency management - all commands should be run with `uv run python`. Django admin is at `/admin` when `manage.py runserver` is active. Configure DB with `DATABASE_URL`; Redis must run for Celery. Production use requires proper secret management and database configuration.
